dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: lehanāmanthanākoṭaiḥ strīsukhasya bharāt smṛteḥ | śaktyabhāve 'pi deveśi bhaved ānandasamplavaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: O Goddess, even without a partner, through the intensity of remembering the joy of love (its kissing, embracing and caressing), there is a flood of delight.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: since the delight arises from memory alone, without a partner, it is evidently inherent within; it is this inner delight, apart from any partner, that one should meditate on to realise the bliss of divine consciousness. Wallis translates the three nouns hesitantly (marking one with a question mark).
dharana.instruction: Observe only: read and understand this classical description. It is not practised in class.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 70 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the source of that delight, within
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The classical map is a memory releasing a delight that is shown to come from within. Recorded as text only.
geometry.svg_hint: a faint arrow from a remembered scene back to a point within, drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Delight from within (described)
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a delight that seemed to need an outer cause is seen to arise from within. A picture to understand, not an exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the verse: delight that arises from memory alone shows that it is inherent within

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: O Goddess, even without a partner, through the intensity of remembering the joy of love (its kissing, embracing and caressing), there is a flood of delight.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical description: even without a partner, the intense memory of love's pleasures brings a flood of delight; Singh draws the lesson that the delight is inherent within and should be meditated on as such. Observe-only in this school: text to understand, with no practice cues.

honesty.disclosure: Door 047 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 47 (verse 70) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

historical/observe_only: The verse concerns the memory of sexual pleasure. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.
Sexual content: the verse concerns sexual union or its memory. Recorded as classical text only; no practice cues are given.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Not led as a practice. The verse concerns sexual experience; this school records it as classical text only and gives no practice cues. Nothing here is an invitation to any sexual activity in a class setting. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
